overview: This file documents the U.S. State Department’s monitoring of disasters affecting Japan and its territories from 1930 through 1938, including the Izu and Shizuoka earthquakes, typhoons, the Hakodate fire, and major flooding in Tokyo, Kobe, and Taiwan. Diplomatic and consular correspondence records casualties and property losses, checks on American residents and interests, decisions about condolences and relief donations, and Japanese relief, reconstruction, public-health, and flood-control measures. The unusually extensive coverage of the catastrophic July 1938 Kobe flood includes confidential analysis, photographs, press reports, evidence of censorship and understated casualties, accounts of renewed flooding, and discussion of long-term engineering needs. The file also contains several cross-referenced or apparently misfiled records concerning Manchuria, Ethiopian relief, emigration, and later storms.
interest: Shows disasters through diplomatic work: protecting nationals, calibrating sympathy, and relief gifts; Kobe reports reveal minimization and information control.
